correctness.rationale: Before threshold activation, direct induction gives y^k=-(kb/(1+a^2))(1,a) and Ry^k=((k+2)b/(1+a^2))(1,a). The first-coordinate strict crossing k+2>gamma(1+a^2)/b yields the exact floor formula, and gamma>=b/(1-a) ensures the second reflected coordinate is still within threshold at that first crossing. In the identified cell the error matrix is (1/(1+a^2))[[a^2,-a],[a,a^2]], whose transpose product is a^2/(1+a^2) times identity. The entry error lies strictly within the distance-b ball around the reflected fixed point, while all relevant cell-boundary distances are at least b; the reflector is orthogonal on errors and the linear map contracts, so the cell remains invariant. A fresh direct nonlinear replay on a representative parameter set recovered the exact first entry and the package checker tests several further cases. The analytic proof, not finite testing, establishes the continuum claim.

final_claim: For zero-initialized Douglas--Rachford splitting on min |x1|+|x2| subject to x1+a x2=b with 0<a<1, b>0 and gamma>=b/(1-a), the first reflected iterate in the correct sign/support cell is exactly k_*=max{0,floor(gamma(1+a^2)/b)-1}; that cell is invariant thereafter and the Euclidean fixed-point error contracts exactly by a/sqrt(1+a^2) each subsequent step.
